Vs.

full_judgment:
9. Khandaker Mahbub Hossain, learned Counsel for the respondents, on the other hand, has supported the impugned judgment and order. He has further submitted that the plaintiffs predecessor acquired vested right in managing the affairs of the Mosque and the Mazar and enjoying the shirni selat offered therein as they were the Cheragi and the Khademdar thereof and their names were duly recorded in that capacity in the CS, the SA and the RS Khatians. Therefore, their right to manage the affairs of the Mazar and the Mosque and to enjoy the shirni selat offered therein by the devotees cannot be taken away in the name of forming a committee by the outsiders for running the day to day affairs of the Mazar and the Mosque. The High Court Division rightly interfered with the same. In support of his submission, Mr Hossain has referred to the judgments passed in the earlier litigations as mentioned while stating the case of the plaintiffs and the agreement dated 6-3-1922 entered into between the Secretary of State for India in Council and Salimunnessa Bibi, wife of the deceased Khadem and submitted that the appeal be dismissed. 

 17. The plaintiffs case was that since prior to the CS operation, their predecessor, Misir Fakir as the Cheragi and Khadem used to reside in Suit Plot No. 1845/1959 and used to look after and manage the day to day affairs of the Mosque and the Mazar in question and he used to enjoy/appropriate the shirni selat offered by the devotees thereto and except him, none used to look after and manage the Mosque and the Mazar and enjoy the shirni selat offered by the devotees and that Khadem/Cheragi, Misir Fakir, died leaving behind three minor sons named Karan Ali, Museb Ali and Cherag Ali and they had been enjoying the shirni and the gift offered to the Mosque and the Mazar through their mother, Salimunnessa and after they had attained majority, they were enjoying the shirni selat. It needs to be mentioned that in the meantime, Cherag Ali died leaving behind plaintiff Nos. 2-4. In support of their case, the plaintiffs besides producing oral evidence filed the CS khatian which was marked as exhibit-T in the CS Khatian, the names of the plaintiffs predecessor, namely, Karan Ali, Museb Ali and Cherag Ali were recorded as Cheragi. The CS record shows that the Mosque in question is situated in CS Plot No. 1845 and CS Plot No.1845/1959 has been recorded as graveyard. In the SA Khatian, the name of Museb Ali and Cherag Ali, sons of Misir Fakir, have been recorded as the Khadem of the Mosque and the Mazar (in the khatian, in Bangla, it has been recorded as “মালিক দং হযরত কুতুবূদ্দিন আউলিয়া সাহেবের মসজিদ ও মাজার পক্ষে খাদেম মুছাবালা চেরাগ আলী পিং মিছির ফকির সাং অষ্টগ্রাম।”) 

 18. In the RS Khatian, the names of Museb Ali and Cherag Ali have also been recorded as Khademdar on behalf of Archaeology Department of the Government of Bangladesh (in Bangla, it has been recorded asদং বাংলাদেশ সরকার প্রন্তত্ত্ব বিভাগ পক্ষে খাদেমের (১) মুছের আলী (২) চেরাগ আলী পিং মিছির আলী সাং নিজ। 

 21. As stated earlier, in fact, the plaintiffs filed the suit challenging the legality of the committee formed by the Upazila Nirbahi Officer and approved by the Deputy Commissioner for the management of the Mazar and the Mosque and running their day to day affairs. Their whole claim was that since prior to the CS khatian, their predecessor had been performing the job of Cheragi/Khadem of the Mosque and the Mazar in question and managing their day to day affairs and enjoying the shirni selat offered thereto and on the death of their predecessor, it is they who have been enjoying/appropriating the shirni selat offered to the Mazar and the Mosque by the devotees and their names were accordingly recorded in the CS khatian, the SA khatian and the RS khatian and by forming the committee challenged in the suit, they were being deprived of their said right. With the additional paper book filed on behalf of the plaintiff-respondents, the CS khatian, the SA khatian and the RS khatians have been incorporated. The CS khatian and the RS khatians have got presumptive value and in these two khatians, the name of Museb Ali, plaintiff No. 1 and the name of Cherag Ali, father of plaintiff Nos.2-4 were recorded as the Cheragi and Khademdar respectively, so the claim of the plaintiffs that they had been managing and running the day to day affairs of the Mosque and the Mazar and they had been enjoying the shirni selat offered by the devotees to the Mazar and the Mosque could not be disbelieved. That the plaintiffs had been managing and running the day to day affairs of the Mazar and the Mosque and that they had been enjoying/appropriating the shirni selat offered by the devotees are also apparent from the fact that in 1934, they filed a suit for permanent injunction against Sheikh Mannan, son of late Sheikh Katan Fakir and Sheikh Thandu who were creating disturbance in their enjoyment of shirni selat of the Mazar in question and the said suit ended on the basis of an award in favour of the plaintiffs. The judgment and decree of the said suit was filed in the trial Court and was proved and marked as exhibit-'3' The said award reads as follows: 

 23. It further appears that the suit land was wrongly recorded in the ROR khatian in the name of one Abdul Hakim and then Museb Ali Fakir (plaintiff No. 1) and Cherag Ali Fakir, predecessor-in-interest or plaintiff Nos. 2-4 filed Miscellaneous Case No. 12 of 1972 for correction of the record under section 143A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. The case was dismissed against which the petitioners filed Miscellaneous Appeal No. 202 of 1974 before the District Judge, Mymensingh and the appeal was allowed and the miscellaneous case was allowed and the name of the said Abdul Hakim was deleted and the record was corrected pursuant to the judgment passed in the miscellaneous appeal. All these facts prima facie show that it is the plaintiffs, who, in fact, had been managing the Mosque and the Mazar and running their day to day affairs and enjoying/appropriating the shirni selat offered therein. 

 25. From the judgment of the trial Court as jotted down hereinbefore, it is abundantly clear that, in considering the case of the plaintiffs that since prior to the CS Khatian, their predecessor who was the Khadem /Cheragi of the Mosque and the Mazar used to manage thereof and run their day to day affairs and enjoy the shirni selat offered thereto and after his death, Salimunnessa, widow of the Khadem, managed the Mosque and the Mazar and run their day to day affairs on behalf of the minors and that after they had become major, they managed and enjoyed/appropriated the shirni/selat offered thereto and none else used to manage the Mazar and the Mosque and enjoy and appropriate the shirni selat and, in fact, there was no committee for the management of the Mosque and the Mazar before the approval of the committee by the Deputy Commissioner under challenge totally failed to consider the material documentary evidence, such as, the CS Khatian (exhibit-'1'), the judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No.1251 of 1934 (exhibit-'3') and the judgment passed in Miscellaneous Appeal No.202 of 1974(exhibit-'4') and the other documents, such as, the SA Khatian and the RS Khatians. Though the trial Court considered the agreement dated 6-3-1922, it wrongly discarded the same. The trial Court totally failed to comprehend the case of the plaintiffs and dismissed the suit taking into consideration some extraneous matters on the wrong assumption of fact holding that ‘চাকর’ of the Mosque or under a Mosque committee (though except the committee under challenge the defendants failed to prove that previously there was any committee for the management of the Mosque and the Mazar in question) could not have any title of the suit land and that the Zumma Mosque could not be under the private ownership completely forgetting the rebel sought in the suit and also the further broad admitted fact that the Mosque in question was declared as ancient monument and the gazette to that effect was made as back as on 25th August, 1909 in the Eastern Bengal and Asam Gazette by the then Government of Bengal under section 3(1) of Act No. VII of 1904 and now it is the Archaeological Department of the Government of Bangladesh which is protecting /preserving it under the provisions of the Antiquities Act, 1968 and in the R:S Khatian, it has been clearly recorded as "দং বাংলাদেশ সরকার প্রন্তত্ব্ব বিভাগ পক্ষে খাদেমদার (১) মুছের আলী (২) চেরাগ আলী পিং মিছির আলী. And since it is the Cheragi/ Khademdar who were managing the Mosque and the Mazar and running their day to day affairs, their names were correctly recorded in the CS khatian and also in the SA recording of their names has nothing to do with the offering of salat/namaj in the Mosque which was established as back as in 16th hundred century. It may be mentioned that in the RS khatian, the Mosque has been recorded in the name of the Government of Bangladesh, Archaeology Department and the names of the Khademdars have been recorded on their behalf. And merely because the names of the Khadems were recorded in the CS, the SA and the RS khatians, the Mosque did not become a mosque under a private ownership, In this regard, the Appellate Court made unnecessary referehce to paragraphs 218 and 188 of the Mohammadan Law while concurring with the view of the trial Court. Both the Courts below failed to consider that there was no dispute as to the offering prayer in the Mosque. The Appellate Court in an oblique reference held that recording of the suit land in the name of Museb Ali and others was wrong because Khadem of a Mosque is a servant, so their names could be recorded as possessor (দখলকার). The reasoning of the Appellate Court is absolutely erroneous and misconceived. Since it is plaintiff No. 1, the predecessor of plaintiff Nos. 2-4 and deceased Karan, who were managing and running the day to day affairs of the Mosque and the Mazar, their names were recorded as the Cheragi thereof in the CS Khatian. The Appellate Court also failed to consider that in the SA and the RS khatians, possession was shown in the name of Hazrat Kutubuddin Aulia Shaheb Mosque and Mazar and the Government of Bangladesh, Department of Archaeology respectively and the plaintiffs were shown as the Khademdars only and by such recording the character of the Mosque as an ancient monument was not lost and it did not become a mosque under private ownership.
